main_text.p: l. 1. in init. D. de Abigeis. l. quicunque. Cod. de serv. fugitiv.alacrius in illos animad-vertatur. Crescente enim malitiâ, etiam crescere con-venit poenas: & ubi frequen-tius est maleficii genus, ibi id durissime vindicandum. In tantum etiam, ut fustigatione, infamiâ, aliisque poenarum generibus essent coercendi, qui sine modo ac mensurâ convicia in quempiam jacere soliti. Ita enim optime Rectores rempublicam administrabunt, & conscientiae consulent. Idque Plutarch, in Apophth. Lacon. in Theopomp.ex illo Theopompi. Qui ro-gatus, quomodo securissime regnum tueri posset, respondit si amicis libertatem justa lo-quendi concesserit, & subdi-tos, qui injuria afficiuntur pro viribus non neglexerit.
Hoc si usu obtineret, non adeo audacter & licentiosè conviciatores, qui responsò digni non sunt, in virorum bonorum famam grassarentur.

page.notes: The page has one text column and marginal notes in the left margin only. The left-margin notes are split by line-end hyphens and by a break in "Apo / phth." and "La / con."; I joined them as "Apophth." and "Lacon." because no hyphen is printed at the break. The accent on "responsò" is hard to read and may be a grave accent or a different mark. The watermark in the lower right corner belongs to the digitiser and is left out. The bottom centre rule is part of the scan edge and is left out.
